hotwire.update.breaks_user: %s uses %s, which version %s no longer has, so it would crash with it. Update %s first, or keep the version you have.
hotwire.add.starts_before_world: It sets itself up as the game starts, before any world opens. Hotwire will save your world, close it, add the mod, and reopen it
hotwire.add.starts_refused: %s sets itself up as the game starts, before any world opens. %s
hotwire.add.starts_use_reopen: %s sets itself up as the game starts, before any world opens. Use Save and add to save your world, add the mod, and reopen the world.
hotwire.add.makes_use_reopen: %s makes %s, which a world only loads when it opens. Use Save and add to save your world, add the mod, and reopen the world.
hotwire.reopen.single_player_only: Save and add only works in a single-player world. On a server, add it from the title screen.
hotwire.reopen.lan: This world is open to LAN, so it can't be closed for the add! Close it to LAN, or add the mod from the title screen.
hotwire.reopen.not_reopened: The world didn't reopen (%s). Please open it from the world list.
hotwire.switch.lunar: Unfortunately Hotwire is incompatible with Lunar Client due to it's obfuscation. My deepest apologies sweetheart ): - Irene/Moonshee
hotwire.next_start.add: %s %s goes in when you close the game. Cancel it any time from Pending tasks.
hotwire.next_start.update: %s updates to %s when you close the game. Cancel it any time from Pending tasks.
hotwire.next_start.why: It goes in at your next start, this game won't let Hotwire change mods while it runs.
hotwire.update.same: You already have this version of %s.
hotwire.update.unreadable_jar: That jar couldn't be read as a mod.
hotwire.switch.no_instrument: This game won't let Hotwire change mods while it runs, so switching, adding and live updates are off. Your mods still load as usual when you start the game.
hotwire.reopen.why.off_server: These can't be turned off while you're on this server.
hotwire.reopen.why.on_server: These can't be turned on while you're on this server.
hotwire.reopen.why.off_world: These can't be turned off while your world is open.
hotwire.reopen.why.on_world: These can't be turned on while your world is open.
hotwire.report.crash_title: This crash was caused by Hotwire
hotwire.report.crash_blame: Report it to Hotwire ONLY, NOT to any mod's developer!
hotwire.report.show_ask: Open the folder with that file now?
hotwire.add.pick: Pick the mod's .jar file, or drop it onto this screen.
hotwire.update.pick: Pick the newer .jar file, or drop it onto this screen.
hotwire.add.world_open: It can't be added while your world is open.
hotwire.add.start_only: Part of it can only start together with the game.
hotwire.add.finishes_at_join: It's in! Part of it only starts when you join a world, so it will finish on your next join.
hotwire.screen.no_picker: No file picker opened on this system. Please drop the .jar file onto this screen instead.
hotwire.self_change: Hotwire can't add, update or turn off itself while it runs! Put the new jar in your mods folder and restart the game.
hotwire.off_code.world: It's off, but your world still holds things it made while it was on. Reopen the world to clear them.
hotwire.off_code.ran: %s is off, but some of its code just ran. Hotwire couldn't take all of it out. %s
hotwire.off_code.restart: Turn it back on to make it whole again, or restart the game to clear it.
hotwire.off_code.used_by: %1$s is off, but %2$s still runs its code. Turn %2$s off too to clear it. From now on it will go off with %1$s.
hotwire.off_code.reopen: Save and reopen your world to clear what it holds. Restart the game to clear all of it.
hotwire.crash.title: Hotwire caught a crash
hotwire.crash.off_held: %s is off, but a piece of it the game still had crashed. Hotwire kept the game going. Restart the game to clear it. %s
hotwire.crash.turned_off: %s crashed, so Hotwire turned it off. The game will carry on. %s
hotwire.crash.not_turned_off: %s crashed and couldn't be turned off: %s %s
hotwire.own_fault.title: Hotwire caught a fault of its own
hotwire.own_fault: Hotwire's own code failed inside the game, but the game carried on: %s. Please restart the game to be safe. %s
hotwire.report.about: Something went wrong? Make a report: one zip file with the game log and what Hotwire did.
hotwire.settings.question: Got a question?
hotwire.report.title: Your bug report is ready
hotwire.report.failure_title: That didn't work, so Hotwire wrote a bug report
hotwire.report.send: Send that file to wherever you got Hotwire from. Nothing is sent automatically.
hotwire.report.holds: It holds the game log and what Hotwire did, with your name and login taken out.
hotwire.report.failed: The bug report couldn't be written: %s
hotwire.update.also: Also updates %s to %s, which it carries.
hotwire.picker.title: Add a mod
modmenu.descriptionTranslation.hotwire: Turn mods off and on, add and update them, all while the game runs.
hotwire.switch.hint.session: It will *turn back on* when you restart the game unless you change that in Settings.
hotwire.store.no_version: %s has no version for your Minecraft and Fabric.
hotwire.store.needs_no_version: it needs %s, which has no version for your Minecraft and Fabric
hotwire.store.pack.downloaded: %s is downloaded. Turn it on with its switch.
hotwire.store.pack.shader_needs_iris: Shaders require Iris! Get it in the Mods tab first.
hotwire.dev.needs_restart.line: This build goes in when you restart the game
hotwire.dev.restored: %s and your files are back on build %s
hotwire.dev.restored.undo: Your files from before are kept, Undo puts them back
hotwire.dev.restore.other_branch: Made on branch %s, you are on %s: restoring puts its code here as changes not committed
hotwire.dev.restored.unseen: %s was left as it is: it changed after this build was compiled, before Hotwire could keep its code
hotwire.dev.restore.no_sources: Build %s kept no sources, it was made before builds kept them
hotwire.dev.restore.failed: Your files could not be written: %s
hotwire.dev.undone: %s's files are back as they were before the restore
hotwire.dev.undone.build: Build to put them into the game
hotwire.dev.rolled_back.from: Rolled back from build %s, which stays kept
hotwire.dev.rolled_back.start: %s is back on the build the game started with
hotwire.dev.waiting: Your newest build waits until you resume reloads
hotwire.dev.unreadable_file: %s couldn't be read, so this build waits for your next one
hotwire.dev.window.title: Developer
hotwire.dev.window.off: Developer mode works when you run the game from your mod's dev setup with Reload when you build on
hotwire.dev.window.no_mods: No mod here runs from its build folders
hotwire.dev.window.started_with: Running the build the game started with
hotwire.dev.window.no_history: Nothing yet. Build your mod and what happens shows up here
hotwire.dev.cleared.back: Bring them back in Manage builds until the game closes
hotwire.dev.manage.title: Manage builds: all %s take %s
hotwire.dev.manage.pick: Tick builds to clear them, or pick some below
hotwire.dev.manage.pick_older: Every build older than an hour
hotwire.dev.manage.bring_back: Bring back the %s cleared this session
hotwire.dev.manage.pinned_warning: A pinned build is ticked. Clear waits 3 seconds before it goes
hotwire.dev.compare.title: A/B: build %s against build %s
hotwire.dev.compare.hint.no_key: Set a key in the developer window to switch
hotwire.dev.compare.bar: A/B of builds %s and %s. Stop and go back to build %s
hotwire.dev.compare.stopped: Stopped, the game is back on your code's build
hotwire.dev.compare.no_flip: Build %s could not go in live, its classes changed shape (the JetBrains Runtime takes it)
hotwire.dev.why.title: Your methods, B against A
hotwire.dev.button.restore.start: Restore the start build, code too
hotwire.dev.trying: Trying build %s, your code is at build %s. Back to it
hotwire.dev.undo_restore: Your code was restored to build %s. Undo
hotwire.dev.leak: %s still holds the world you left
hotwire.dev.leak.fix: Clear it when the world closes and the whole world can go
hotwire.dev.left_over: Kept running through the off, which a fresh start would not have:
hotwire.dev.left_over.count: %s things of your mod kept running through the off, the window lists them
hotwire.dev.build.back: Click to roll back to it
hotwire.dev.pick.title: Pick a build to go back to. Build %s runs now.
hotwire.dev.report.first: The game started on this build, so there is nothing before it to compare with
hotwire.dev.copy.name: Copy of %s
hotwire.dev.name_hint: Name this build, Enter to save
hotwire.dev.merge.title: Tick the builds to make one
hotwire.dev.merge.how: Their changes become one build. A build you leave out stays as it is.
hotwire.dev.merge.fast: Build %s takes in builds %s, as it is
hotwire.dev.merge.why_kept: Build %s is newer, so its version stays and build %s's goes
hotwire.dev.merge.left_why: Build %s was made on build %s. The merge won't have these changes of it:
hotwire.dev.merge.stays_running: Build %s runs now, so it stays as it is too
hotwire.dev.merge.stays_pinned: Build %s is pinned, so it stays as it is too
hotwire.dev.merge.goes: Builds %s are thrown away once merged
hotwire.dev.merge.goes.one: Build %s is thrown away once merged
hotwire.dev.merge.game: The game keeps running what it runs. Roll back to the merge to try it.
hotwire.dev.merge.start: The start can't be merged, every build comes from it
hotwire.dev.merge.no_record: Hotwire has no record of what build %s changed
hotwire.dev.merge.base_gone: These builds split at build %s, which is no longer kept
hotwire.dev.merge.unwritten: The merged build could not be written
hotwire.dev.merge.kept_newer: Kept the newer version of %s files
hotwire.dev.auto_back.why: Build %s threw %s at %s, so Hotwire rolled it back. Turn this off in Settings, Developer.
hotwire.dev.pick.start: The build the game started with
hotwire.dev.mcp.get: Coding agents can use all of this too
hotwire.dev.mcp.get.line: Get the Hotwire MCP mod from our GitHub releases and put it next to Hotwire, click here to open them
hotwire.dev.half: %s isn't a whole class file, so the build waits for your next one
hotwire.dev.start_changed: %s's start code changed, so what it registers there comes in at the next start
hotwire.dev.fields_added: New fields in %s show to config and save libraries after a restart, or right away on the JetBrains Runtime
hotwire.dev.elsewhere: %s runs outside the mod loader, so this change to it waits for a restart
hotwire.dev.crash.open: Click to open it in your IDE
hotwire.dev.copied: No IDE answered, so the place is copied
